Charles-Marie Gustave Le Bon [ a ] (7 May 1841 – 13 December 1931) was a leading French polymath whose areas of interest included anthropology , psychology , sociology , medicine , invention, and physics . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] He is best known for his 1895 work The Crowd: A Study of the Popular Mind , which is considered one of the seminal works of crowd psychology . [ 4 ] [ 5 ]
